properties.chose: Anthony, 2026-10-30: "Go with your recommendation". Kept (a): the gates are the protocol of the proof calibration (increment 4), measured with and without them (req:the-proof-calibration-holds-the-agents-attempt-to-mechanical-gates-with-and-without). Kept (b), conditional on that measurement: reflow2 pins an attempt and reports statement or axiom drift and steps closed per round (req:reflow2-reports-when-a-proof-attempts-statement-or-axioms-moved-during-it). (c) a step reads machine-checked only with a checker's record, and (d) a fresh second agent audits each closed step, stay considered.
properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-10-30, as a /brainstorm: "I'd like to look into https://arxiv.org/html/2608.00965v1 / https://www.wired.com/story/software-verification-is-the-hot-new-answer-to-the-ai-safety-crisis/ and see if there is anything we can take from this - this might be something more for flo2-calc?"

WHAT THE PAPER DID (CryptoProver, Sun, Fong, Kuang, Jiao, Narodytska, Wu, Dill, Barrett; Stanford/UNC/VMware/Amherst, read 2026-10-30): a Python driver loop hands proof search to a general coding agent (Claude Code), which writes the intermediate specifications and proofs for a production Rust crypto crate; Verus (SMT, Z3) checks the crate. People supply the top-level API contracts, the specification vocabulary and the trusted library; the agent writes everything between. Its principle: the driver accepts progress ONLY from verifier output, admit counts and gate evidence, never from the agent's self-report ("rules without gates are only suggestions"). Eight mechanical gates, among them: admit-count (each round removes at least one unproved obligation), axiom-drift (no new axioms), spec-drift (the top-level statement byte-identical to its state at the start), sibling-verus (edited files and their neighbours still verify), git-recovery (the agent may not read the answer from history). Fresh sessions per attempt, and a reset when progress stalls or context grows too large. Results: curve25519-dalek 2,031 checks verified, 0 errors, 11.4 h, about $467; the same model WITHOUT the driver and gates stopped after 7.4 h and $1,117 claiming success with 7 errors left. An earlier campaign's claimed 97.1% hid 11 "proofs" resting on invented axioms; an audit found them. Limits the paper states: correctness only against the contracts people wrote; single runs; tuned on the crate it reports. The Wired article could not be fetched here (blocked); a search shows it covers automated formal verification startups (e.g. &Truth) and the spec problem: someone must first say precisely what the software should do.

WHAT reflow2 ALREADY HAS: who confirmed each inference step (person, checker, unconfirmed: cap:proof-who-confirmed); proof_status and foundations on a conclusion (the axioms it rests on); a claim made by a named party reads claimed; a test's criteria changed after its data arrived is reported (req:a-change-to-a-tests-criteria-after-its-data-arrived-is-reported). The plan already has the proof track: increment 4 calibrates on a known answer, fresh agent per round; increment 5 works one named hole. What it lacks is the ATTEMPT as a thing with a start: nothing says "the statement or the axioms moved during this attempt", and nothing counts holes closed per round.

OPTIONS, none chosen:
(a) GATES AS THE PROTOCOL ONLY: increment 4 and 5 run with these gates checked by the harness (as the recall pilot was scored blind), nothing built in reflow2.
(b) reflow2 READS THE GATES: an attempt is pinned at its start (statement, givens, axioms, open holes); reflow2 reports statement drift, axiom drift (a new foundation since the pin), and holes closed per round, the way the criteria lock is reported for a test.
(c) A STEP READS PROVEN ONLY WITH A CHECKER'S RECORD ATTACHED: an inference step confirmed by `checker` must carry the checker's kept output (a calc record, a Lean or SMT log, by checksum); a step the agent says it checked, with nothing attached, reads unconfirmed.
(d) THE AUDIT AS A SECOND AGENT: a fresh agent, never shown the first's reasoning, re-derives or attacks each closed hole (the paper's fresh-context repair; ties to dec:idea-what-makes-a-finished-proof-trustworthy-to-a-person).

PUSHBACK, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
- MUCH OF THIS IS ALREADY NAMED. foundations, who-confirmed and the criteria lock cover most of (b) and (c) in pieces; the gain is the attempt window and the counts, not new vocabulary.
- THE PAPER HAD A REAL CHECKER (Verus). reflow2 is not one: on mathematics without a formal checker, gates can stop drift and false claims of progress, but cannot make a step true. Only (c) with a real checker, or a person, does that.
- SPEC-DRIFT IS THE CHEAP, HIGH-VALUE ONE. It is the failure our own trials met in another shape (an agent quietly narrowing what it claims), and it needs only a pin and a comparison.
- SINGLE RUNS, TUNED ON ONE TARGET: the paper's numbers say gates help a lot once; they don't yet say how much in general. Our increment 4 is the place to measure it, with and without the gates.

COST (a finding): (a) none to build; (b) small to moderate (a pin plus three computed readings, on records reflow2 already keeps); (c) small for the rule, the checker itself is the cost (see the flo2-calc idea); (d) the cost of one more agent per hole.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-30 — an agent's proof attempt is held to mechanical gates: as the calibration's protocol now (a), and read by reflow2 itself if the calibration shows it matters (b); the checker's record on each step (c) and a second-agent audit (d) stay considered
properties.rationale:
Anthony asked what we can take from CryptoProver and the Wired piece on AI-driven formal verification. The paper's central lesson (accept progress only from mechanical evidence, never from the agent's report) matches what this design measured itself (a self-reported count 0 that blind-scored 5.5 in the reading-budget run; a piped gate's false green) and lands on the proof track already planned (increments 4 and 5). Recorded as the open part: whether reflow2 should know an attempt and read its gates.
